Synopsis:
    US Treasury bonds sold off again after a brief relief rally, pushing 30Y yields to 5.247%
    and 10Y to 4.70%, as markets questioned the durability of Treasury buyback measures.
    Equities were broadly weak — Nasdaq -1%, S&P 500 -0.9% — pressured by rising yields and
    elevated oil prices (Brent +2% to $93.49), with Strait of Hormuz disruption a key driver.
    Fed minutes flagged deepening inflation concern, with several members open to hikes and
    many conditioning hikes on failure to reach 2% target. AI/semiconductor stocks bucked
    the trend. The dollar was marginally higher; the yen weakened to 159.12.
